file.content:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install Rust toolchain & cache (matches rust-toolchain.toml's pin)
        uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@v1.1
        with:
          components: clippy,rustfmt

      # just and cargo-deny have no working proto plugin; install them directly.
      # Same arrangement as Lumen and Michi.
      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@v2

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Run CI pipeline
        run: just ci

1	# Default recipe: run full CI pipeline via moon & just
2	default: ci
3	
4	# ── Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5	build:
6	    moon run :build
7	
8	build-release:
9	    cargo build --release --workspace
10	
11	build-node:
12	    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm build --platform
13	
14	build-node-release:
15	    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm build --platform --release
16	
17	# ── Test ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
18	test:
19	    moon run :test
20	
21	test-rust:
22	    cargo nextest run --workspace
23	
24	test-rust-all:
25	    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features
26	
27	# Each published crate alone with its default features: a workspace-wide run unifies features across crates.
28	test-crates-default:
29	    cargo nextest run -p michi-core
30	    cargo nextest run -p michi-graph
31	    cargo nextest run -p michi-pipeline
32	
33	# The fixed group's semver release type from pending changesets (front matter only).
34	pending-release-type:
35	    python3 scripts/pending-release-type.py "$(grep -m1 '^version' crates/michi-core/Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/version *= *"(.*)"/\1/')"
36	
37	# michi-graph is MIT: fail if a non-permissive license enters its normal or build dependencies.
38	check-graph-license:
39	    python3 scripts/test_check_permissive_deps.py
40	    cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features | python3 scripts/check-permissive-deps.py michi-graph
41	
42	# Post-release check: install a *published* version from npm and crates.io into clean projects and use it.
43	# Needs network. `SMOKE_RETRY_SECONDS` (default 600) bounds the wait for the registries.
44	smoke-published version:
45	    scripts/smoke-published.sh {{version}}
46	
47	test-rust-release:
48	    cargo nextest run --workspace --release
49	
50	test-node: build-node
51	    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm test
52	
53	# ── Lint & Format ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
54	check: fmt-check clippy doc-check fuzz-check zizmor deny typos fmt-md-check
55	
56	# Static security audit of the workflows (needs zizmor 1.29.0, the version CI runs).
57	zizmor:
58	    zizmor --offline .github
59	
60	# Compile the fuzz targets on stable. fuzz/ is outside the workspace, so nothing else builds it; CI does the same.
61	fuzz-check:
62	    cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins
63	
64	lint:
65	    moon run :lint
66	
67	# Affected-only lint: uses moon's dependency-graph-aware affected-project
68	# detection to build the crate scope, then feeds it into ONE cargo
69	# invocation with multiple -p flags. This is the incremental counterpart to
70	# `lint` (which lints the whole workspace in one shot) -- it exists so a
71	# pre-push hook doesn't have to choose between "lint everything every time"
72	# and "fan out one cargo process per crate" (the latter serializes behind
73	# Cargo's shared target/ lock; see .moon/tasks/rust.yml). Only lints the
74	# affected crates' own source, not their downstream dependents -- clippy
75	# warnings are about a crate's own code, not its callers.

# Default recipe: run full CI pipeline via moon & just
default: ci

# ── Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
    moon run :build

build-release:
    cargo build --release --workspace

build-node:
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm build --platform

build-node-release:
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm build --platform --release

# ── Test ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
    moon run :test

test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace

test-rust-all:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features

# Each published crate alone with its default features: a workspace-wide run unifies features across crates.
test-crates-default:
    cargo nextest run -p michi-core
    cargo nextest run -p michi-graph
    cargo nextest run -p michi-pipeline

# The fixed group's semver release type from pending changesets (front matter only).
pending-release-type:
    python3 scripts/pending-release-type.py "$(grep -m1 '^version' crates/michi-core/Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/version *= *"(.*)"/\1/')"

# michi-graph is MIT: fail if a non-permissive license enters its normal or build dependencies.
check-graph-license:
    python3 scripts/test_check_permissive_deps.py
    cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features | python3 scripts/check-permissive-deps.py michi-graph

# Post-release check: install a *published* version from npm and crates.io into clean projects and use it.
# Needs network. `SMOKE_RETRY_SECONDS` (default 600) bounds the wait for the registries.
smoke-published version:
    scripts/smoke-published.sh {{version}}

test-rust-release:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --release

test-node: build-node
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm test

# ── Lint & Format ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
check: fmt-check clippy doc-check fuzz-check zizmor deny typos fmt-md-check

# Static security audit of the workflows (needs zizmor 1.29.0, the version CI runs).
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline .github

# Compile the fuzz targets on stable. fuzz/ is outside the workspace, so nothing else builds it; CI does the same.
fuzz-check:
    cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins

lint:
    moon run :lint

# Affected-only lint: uses moon's dependency-graph-aware affected-project
# detection to build the crate scope, then feeds it into ONE cargo
# invocation with multiple -p flags. This is the incremental counterpart to
# `lint` (which lints the whole workspace in one shot) -- it exists so a
# pre-push hook doesn't have to choose between "lint everything every time"
# and "fan out one cargo process per crate" (the latter serializes behind
# Cargo's shared target/ lock; see .moon/tasks/rust.yml). Only lints the
# affected crates' own source, not their downstream dependents -- clippy
# warnings are about a crate's own code, not its callers.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id // empty')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No affected crates; skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    # Root-level changes (manifests, toolchain, lint config) affect every crate.
    if grep -qx michi-workspace <<< "$projects"; then
        echo "Workspace root affected; linting every crate."
        cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    while IFS= read -r p; do
        args+=(-p "$p")
    done <<< "$projects"
    echo "Linting affected crates: ${args[*]}"
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

clippy:
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings

fmt:
    moon run :format

format: fmt

fmt-check:
    moon run :format-check

fmt-md:
    CI=true pnpm exec oxfmt --ignore-path=.oxfmtignore --write "**/*.md"

fmt-md-check:
    CI=true pnpm exec oxfmt --ignore-path=.oxfmtignore --check "**/*.md"

typos:
    typos

deny:
    cargo deny check

audit:
    moon run :audit

# ── Documentation Checks ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
doc: doc-check

doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features
    # Default features alone: intra-doc links to feature-gated items only break here.
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p michi-core --no-deps

# API SemVer check of the published crates against their latest crates.io release (the default baseline). CI runs the
# same check.
check-api:
    bash scripts/check-semver.sh

# Unused-dependency check.
machete:
    cargo machete

# ── Examples & Benchmarks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
examples:
    moon run :examples

example name:
    cargo run -p michi-core --example {{name}}

snapshots:
    cargo insta review

snapshots-accept:
    cargo insta test --accept

bench:
    cargo bench --workspace

bench-baseline:
    cargo bench --workspace -- --save-baseline main

# Mutation testing sweep, workspace-wide. Complements the per-task mutation
# checks the implementation workflow already runs during development
# (surviving mutants get precision tests before a task's exit gate) with a
# standing, repeatable local/CI command over the whole tree.
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# ── Fuzzing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Run one cargo-fuzz target from fuzz/ for `seconds` (default 60). Needs `rustup toolchain install nightly` and
# `cargo install cargo-fuzz --locked`. Targets: toon_render truncate resilience mcp_wire graph plan. Not part of
# `check` or `ci`: fuzz/ is outside the workspace and a bounded run proves nothing by passing.
fuzz target seconds="60":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    test -f "fuzz/fuzz_targets/{{target}}.rs" || { echo "no such target: {{target}}"; ls fuzz/fuzz_targets; exit 1; }
    args=("fuzz/corpus/{{target}}")
    mkdir -p "fuzz/corpus/{{target}}"
    if [ -d "fuzz/seeds/{{target}}" ]; then args+=("fuzz/seeds/{{target}}"); fi
    opts=(-max_total_time={{seconds}})
    if [ -f "fuzz/dictionaries/{{target}}.dict" ]; then opts+=("-dict=fuzz/dictionaries/{{target}}.dict"); fi
    # cargo-fuzz defaults --target to its own build's triple. CI installs a musl build of it, and nightly rejects the
    # address sanitizer on statically linked musl, so build for the nightly toolchain's host instead.
    host=$(rustc +nightly -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')
    cargo +nightly fuzz run --target "$host" "{{target}}" "${args[@]}" -- "${opts[@]}"

# ── Continuous Development ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
watch:
    cargo watch -x "check --workspace --all-features"

# ── Coverage & Cleanup ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
coverage:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info

clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean
    rm -f lcov.info

# ── Git Hooks & Pre-push ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
pre-commit: fmt-check

pre-push: fmt-check lint-affected

hooks:
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-commit' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-push' > .git/hooks/pre-push
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push
    @echo "Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks installed successfully."

# ── CI Verification Pipeline ───────────────────────────────────────────────
check-all: ci

ci: fmt-check lint test test-rust-release audit doc-check

file.content:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  INSTA_UPDATE: "no"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

jobs:
  # Cheap, standalone check that .prototools is fully proto-installable.
  # This is the ONLY thing in this file that exercises the same
  # moonrepo/setup-toolchain -> proto install path callisto-release.yml's
  # Callisto actions use internally -- without this job, .prototools could
  # break silently and only surface at actual release time (which is what
  # happened: multiple tools here had no working proto plugin, and CI
  # stayed green through all of it since nothing here ever touched proto).
  prototools:
    name: .prototools is installable
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4

  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          components: rustfmt,clippy
      - run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: typos
        uses: crate-ci/typos@7f9d0819ca1c008ade73f4b41fa9d258d48f605b # v1.51.1

  docs:
    name: Docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features
      # Default features on their own: intra-doc links to feature-gated items only break here.
      - run: cargo doc -p michi-core --no-deps

  markdown:
    name: Markdown format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: CI=true pnpm exec oxfmt --ignore-path=.oxfmtignore --check "**/*.md"

  semver:
    name: SemVer (against crates.io)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@86f7a0ffb25f40114606501a311ebcfaf882ea32 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-semver-checks
      # The baseline is the latest version of each crate published on crates.io. The release type comes from the
      # pending changesets, translated to cargo-semver-checks' terms: it names release types literally, so a breaking
      # change needs `major` even before 1.0, where Callisto's minor bump (0.3 -> 0.4) is the breaking bump.
      - run: python3 scripts/test_pending_release_type.py
      - name: Check API compatibility against the pending release type
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Front matter of the fixed group's changesets, or the version bump when none are pending, as on Callisto's
          # version PR.
          bash scripts/check-semver.sh

  # Spec first: a PR that changes public Rust API must also touch the docs (docs/spec, docs/adr, a README or
  # ARCHITECTURE.md), or say why not with a `No spec change needed: <reason>` line in the PR body. The body is read
  # live, so after editing it, re-run this job.
  api-docs:
    name: Spec updated with API changes
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: python3 scripts/test_check_api_docs.py
      - run: python3 scripts/test_released_version.py
      - name: Check the spec moves with the API
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_URL: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PR_BODY="$(gh pr view "$PR_URL" --json body --jq .body)"
          export PR_BODY
          python3 scripts/check-api-docs.py "origin/$BASE_REF" HEAD

  msrv:
    name: MSRV
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Read rust-version from Cargo.toml
        id: msrv
        run: echo "version=$(grep -m1 '^rust-version' Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/rust-version *= *"(.*)"/\1/')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}
          cache-key: msrv
      # `+version` because rust-toolchain.toml (stable) would otherwise win over the default toolchain.
      - run: cargo "+$MSRV" check --workspace --all-features --locked
        env:
          MSRV: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}

  fuzz-build:
    name: Fuzz targets build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          cache-key: fuzz-build
      # fuzz/ is outside the workspace, so nothing else compiles it: an API change would break its targets unnoticed.
      # Without --locked: Callisto bumps the michi versions, which the fuzz crate's own lockfile does not follow.
      - run: cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins

  workflow-security:
    name: Workflow security (zizmor)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # Static audit of the workflows: template injection, credential persistence, excessive permissions. The version
      # matches `just zizmor`.
      - run: pipx run zizmor==1.29.0 --offline .github

  graph-license:
    name: michi-graph stays permissive
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: python3 scripts/test_check_permissive_deps.py
      # michi-graph is MIT inside an FSL workspace: no non-permissive crate may enter what it ships.
      - run: cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features | python3 scripts/check-permissive-deps.py michi-graph

  graph-no-std:
    name: michi-graph builds without std
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          targets: thumbv7em-none-eabihf
          cache-key: graph-no-std
      # A bare-metal target with no std: proves the crate is no_std + alloc. It needs pointer-sized atomics (Arc and
      # the builder id), which thumbv7em has; targets without compare-and-swap (thumbv6m) are not supported.
      - run: cargo build -p michi-graph --target thumbv7em-none-eabihf

  version-sync:
    name: Version sync
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - name: Assert every published package has the same version
        run: |
          crate_version() { grep -m1 '^version' "$1" | sed -E 's/version *= *"(.*)"/\1/'; }
          CORE=$(crate_version crates/michi-core/Cargo.toml)
          GRAPH=$(crate_version crates/michi-graph/Cargo.toml)
          PIPELINE=$(crate_version crates/michi-pipeline/Cargo.toml)
          NPM=$(node -p "require('./packages/michi-node/package.json').version")
          echo "michi-core: $CORE  michi-graph: $GRAPH  michi-pipeline: $PIPELINE  @orin-dx/michi: $NPM"
          if [ "$CORE" != "$GRAPH" ] || [ "$CORE" != "$PIPELINE" ] || [ "$CORE" != "$NPM" ]; then
            echo "::error::Version mismatch: michi-core=$CORE michi-graph=$GRAPH michi-pipeline=$PIPELINE @orin-dx/michi=$NPM"
            exit 1
          fi

  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@86f7a0ffb25f40114606501a311ebcfaf882ea32 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,just
      - run: cargo nextest run --workspace
      - run: cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features
      # Each published crate on its own, with only its default features. A workspace-wide run unifies features (the
      # napi shim turns on michi-core's serde), which hid a default-feature failure.
      - run: just test-crates-default
      # nextest does not run doctests (the crate docs and the michi-pipeline and michi-graph README examples).
      # Not `napi`: doctest binaries can't link the Node symbols it references.
      - run: cargo test --doc -p michi-core --features serde,schemars,miette
      - run: cargo test --doc -p michi-pipeline --all-features
      - run: cargo test --doc -p michi-graph

  deny:
    name: Deny
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@3c6349835b2b7b196a839186cb8b78e02f7b5f25 # v2.1.1

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@86f7a0ffb25f40114606501a311ebcfaf882ea32 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov,cargo-nextest
      - run: cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          files: lcov.info
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  bench-build:
    name: Bench (build only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: cargo bench --no-run --workspace

  lint-js:
    name: Lint (JS/TS)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm lint

  napi:
    name: NAPI (${{ matrix.target }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # Every target in packages/michi-node/package.json's napi.targets. `cross`
      # links with cargo-zigbuild, as the release build does for these targets.
      # `test` runs the Node tests only where the runner executes the binary
      # natively: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu builds on GitHub's arm64 runner for
      # that (still linked with cargo-zigbuild, so it tests the release's glibc
      # linkage), and musl or x86_64 macOS binaries can't load in the runner's Node.
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            runner: macos-latest
            test: true
          - target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            runner: macos-latest
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            test: true
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cross: true
          - target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            cross: true
            test: true
          - target: aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cross: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}
          cache-key: ${{ matrix.target }}
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - name: Install ziglang (cross-compile targets only)
        if: matrix.cross
        run: pip install ziglang
      - name: Cache cargo-zigbuild binary (cross-compile targets only)
        if: matrix.cross
        id: zigbuild-cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.cargo/bin/cargo-zigbuild
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-cargo-zigbuild-${{ matrix.target }}
      - name: Install cargo-zigbuild (cross-compile targets only)
        if: matrix.cross && steps.zigbuild-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: cargo install cargo-zigbuild --locked
      - run: pnpm build --target ${{ matrix.target }} ${{ matrix.cross && '--cross-compile' || '' }}
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: node --test __test__/index.test.mjs __test__/interop.test.mjs __test__/mcp-conformance.test.mjs
        working-directory: packages/michi-node

18	
19	- **Untrusted artifact JSON** — `wisp-schema` and `wisp-artifacts` parse `spec@1`/`plan@1`/… documents that may come from an untrusted branch or a malicious agent run. A crafted document that escapes the canonical path (`ArtifactId` rejects `/`, `\`, `.`, `..`), bypasses schema validation, or triggers unbounded resource use is a real finding.
20	- **Repository contents as instructions** — README text, comments, string literals, and copied issue text must never alter Wisp's own validation or persistence policy. Any path by which repository content changes Wisp's behavior beyond being reported as evidence is in scope.
21	- **Persistence and cache integrity** — canonical writes are atomic (tempfile + rename) and hashed after write; `.wisp/` is derived state. A way to make a receipt report `persisted` for bytes that were not written, or to make a stale cache entry validate as current, is in scope.

# Security Policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Email **security@orin-dx.com** — do not open a public issue for anything exploitable before a fix ships.

Include:

- Which crate is affected (`wisp-contracts`, `wisp-model`, `wisp-schema`, `wisp-artifacts`, `wisp-git`, `wisp-monokl`, `wisp-store`, `wisp-context`, `wisp-output`, `wisp-service`, `wisp-cli`, `wisp-mcp`)
- The concrete failure scenario — what an attacker could do, and how
- A sample artifact, workspace layout, or repro steps if you have them (redact anything sensitive first)

Expect an acknowledgment within 5 business days. We will keep you posted as a fix moves through triage and credit you in the release notes unless you would rather stay anonymous.

## Scope

Wisp reads Git-tracked JSON artifacts, inspects Git state, embeds Monokl to analyze source code, and writes canonical artifacts and a local cache. The relevant threat model:

- **Untrusted artifact JSON** — `wisp-schema` and `wisp-artifacts` parse `spec@1`/`plan@1`/… documents that may come from an untrusted branch or a malicious agent run. A crafted document that escapes the canonical path (`ArtifactId` rejects `/`, `\`, `.`, `..`), bypasses schema validation, or triggers unbounded resource use is a real finding.
- **Repository contents as instructions** — README text, comments, string literals, and copied issue text must never alter Wisp's own validation or persistence policy. Any path by which repository content changes Wisp's behavior beyond being reported as evidence is in scope.
- **Persistence and cache integrity** — canonical writes are atomic (tempfile + rename) and hashed after write; `.wisp/` is derived state. A way to make a receipt report `persisted` for bytes that were not written, or to make a stale cache entry validate as current, is in scope.
- **Git subprocess and `gix` argument handling** — `wisp-git` shells out to `git status` and walks history with `gix`. Path or ref arguments that reach the subprocess unescaped are in scope.
- **Embedded Monokl** — `wisp-monokl` runs Monokl's parsers over workspace source. Parser crashes belong to Monokl's policy; Wisp's handling of Monokl errors and partial results belongs here.
- **MCP surface** — `wisp-mcp`'s tool inputs, especially anything that names a path or an artifact id.
- **Supply chain** — the dependency tree, especially `gix`, `rusqlite` if enabled, and anything `unsafe`-adjacent.

The workspace enforces `unsafe_code = "forbid"`. A report showing that lint bypassed, or a memory-safety bug despite it, is a high-priority finding.

Out of scope: issues in Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or other harnesses themselves — report those to the platform.

## Supported versions

Wisp is pre-1.0 and unpublished. Security fixes land on `main` only.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

# Each job runs `just` recipes, so `just ci` locally does what CI does.
jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: clippy,rustfmt
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@8cca0918f8471c33515202b73f56ab27f2bed283 # v2.87.29
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-machete,typos
      - run: just lint doc-check machete typos

  test:
    name: Test / ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@8cca0918f8471c33515202b73f56ab27f2bed283 # v2.87.29
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest
      - run: just test

  msrv:
    name: MSRV
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: msrv
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}
      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@8cca0918f8471c33515202b73f56ab27f2bed283 # v2.87.29
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest,cargo-llvm-cov
      - run: just coverage 90
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: coverage
          path: lcov.info
          retention-days: 14

  audit:
    name: Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@8cca0918f8471c33515202b73f56ab27f2bed283 # v2.87.29
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-deny,zizmor@1.29.0
      - run: just deny zizmor

  changesets:
    name: Changesets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-validate@3feff402ea4798c4708ec6fa09e402b956596598 # callisto@0.14.0

  # The one check to require in branch protection.
  ci:
    name: CI
    needs: [lint, test, msrv, coverage, audit, changesets]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - if: contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') || contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')
        run: exit 1

file.content:
# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install the cargo tools the recipes below use
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install the pinned toolchain and the moon-managed git hooks
setup:
    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the workspace. One `cargo --workspace` invocation, not `moon run :build`: per-crate cargo processes all
# contend for the same target/ lock and serialize.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --locked

build-release:
    cargo build --workspace --release --locked

# Run tests with nextest, plus doctests, which nextest does not run. The default-features pass catches code that only
# builds because --all-features turned something on.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked
    cargo nextest run --workspace --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features --locked

# Line coverage; with a threshold, fails below it
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# Coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

# Format check and clippy, with and without default features
lint:
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features --locked -- -D warnings

# Clippy on the crates moon reports as affected, in one cargo invocation
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

# Documentation build, with warnings (including broken intra-doc links) as errors
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features --locked
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --locked

# Licenses, advisories, bans and sources
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Unused dependencies
machete:
    cargo machete

typos:
    typos

# Callisto config, package discovery and pending changesets; the same gate as CI's Changesets job
changesets:
    callisto status --check
    callisto release --dry-run --format text

# Record a pending change for the next release, e.g. `just changeset minor "Add the search command"`
changeset bump summary:
    callisto add --package cargo/monokl:{{ bump }} --summary "{{ summary }}"

# Workflow audit for permission, credential and supply-chain issues
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Mutation testing. Slow, so on demand only, not part of `just ci`.
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Public API SemVer check against the last published version. Not in `just ci` until a first release exists.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean

# Run by the moon-managed pre-commit hook
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --all --check
    typos

# Run by the moon-managed pre-push hook
pre-push: pre-commit lint-affected

# Everything the CI jobs run
ci: lint test doc-check deny machete typos zizmor changesets (coverage "90")

# Grouped weekly updates, with security updates in their own group so an advisory fix is never hidden in a routine
# bump. The cooldown lets a yanked crate or pulled action release surface before it lands here.
version: 2

updates:
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
    groups:
      routine-actions:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
      security-actions:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

  - package-ecosystem: cargo
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      # oxc_* minor releases carry breaking API changes and ship in lockstep, so they update together. oxc_resolver
      # has its own version line, so it stays out of the group and gets its own PR.
      oxc:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["oxc_*"]
        exclude-patterns: ["oxc_resolver"]
      routine-cargo:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
        exclude-patterns: ["oxc_*"]
      security-cargo:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

content.content:
1	# monokl
2	
3	AST-aware code search for TypeScript, JavaScript and Rust, built for coding agents. Part of [Orin DX](https://orin-dx.com) (github.com/orin-dx). Agent-facing output goes through [michi](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) (`michi-core` on crates.io); don't hand-roll TOON lists, structured errors or hints that michi provides.
4	
5	Vendor-neutral guidance. [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) adds Claude Code specifics.
6	
7	## Read first
8	
9	1. [`docs/spec/README.md`](docs/spec/README.md): which spec file covers what. The spec is the reconstruction source for unbuilt modules.
10	2. [`docs/architecture/README.md`](docs/architecture/README.md): which topic doc to read for the area you're changing.
11	3. [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md) and [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md): decisions already made. If something looks inconsistent, check here before "fixing" it.
12	4. [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md): non-goals. No embedding reranker, no persistent trigram index, no tree-sitter TS/JS parser.
13	
14	## Commands
15	
16	```bash
17	just setup      # proto toolchain + moon git hooks
18	just ci         # everything CI runs
19	just test       # nextest + doctests
20	just lint       # fmt check + clippy, all features and no default features
21	```
22	
23	Run one cargo command at a time; parallel cargo processes serialize on the `target/` lock. Never `git checkout Cargo.lock`.
24	
25	## Current state
26	
27	One crate, `crates/monokl`, with the error types, core data types, query language, text search, ranking, the TypeScript analyzer (parse and extract), the search pipeline and `monokl search`. Modules are declared in `lib.rs` as they are implemented, not ahead of time, and a dependency is listed only once code uses it. [`.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md`](.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md) tracks what's next.
28	
29	## Non-negotiables
30	
31	- No `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!()`/`unreachable!()`/`unimplemented!()` outside `#[cfg(test)]`. The workspace lint table denies them.

# monokl

AST-aware code search for TypeScript, JavaScript and Rust, built for coding agents. Part of [Orin DX](https://orin-dx.com) (github.com/orin-dx). Agent-facing output goes through [michi](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) (`michi-core` on crates.io); don't hand-roll TOON lists, structured errors or hints that michi provides.

Vendor-neutral guidance. [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) adds Claude Code specifics.

## Read first

1. [`docs/spec/README.md`](docs/spec/README.md): which spec file covers what. The spec is the reconstruction source for unbuilt modules.
2. [`docs/architecture/README.md`](docs/architecture/README.md): which topic doc to read for the area you're changing.
3. [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md) and [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md): decisions already made. If something looks inconsistent, check here before "fixing" it.
4. [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md): non-goals. No embedding reranker, no persistent trigram index, no tree-sitter TS/JS parser.

## Commands

```bash
just setup      # proto toolchain + moon git hooks
just ci         # everything CI runs
just test       # nextest + doctests
just lint       # fmt check + clippy, all features and no default features
```

Run one cargo command at a time; parallel cargo processes serialize on the `target/` lock. Never `git checkout Cargo.lock`.

## Current state

One crate, `crates/monokl`, with the error types, core data types, query language, text search, ranking, the TypeScript analyzer (parse and extract), the search pipeline and `monokl search`. Modules are declared in `lib.rs` as they are implemented, not ahead of time, and a dependency is listed only once code uses it. [`.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md`](.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md) tracks what's next.

## Non-negotiables

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!()`/`unreachable!()`/`unimplemented!()` outside `#[cfg(test)]`. The workspace lint table denies them.
- One `thiserror` error enum, `MonoklError`. Compose failure modes with `#[from]`/`#[source]`; no `String`-message variant when a structured one is possible. File I/O failures are `FileIoError` ([ADR 0001](docs/adr/0001-file-io-error-lives-in-monokl.md)).
- `LanguageAnalyzer` implementations return fully owned data. No arena-borrowed AST node or parser-allocator lifetime in any field of `FileAnalysis`.
- `camino::Utf8Path`/`Utf8PathBuf` wherever a path appears.
- `FxHashMap`/`FxHashSet` for internal hot-path maps; `BTreeMap` for anything serialized, because output order must be deterministic.
- Core result types are not `Serialize`; wire shapes live in the output layer. See [`08-library-session-api.md`](docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md#9-plumbing-and-porcelain-two-crates).
- No caps or pre-rendered truncation strings in core. Counts only (`items_returned`/`items_total`); the output layer renders the marker.
- `unsafe_code` is denied workspace-wide.

## Rust style

Skills in [`.agents/skills/`](.agents/skills/) hold the detail: `rust-style` (control flow, matching, naming), `rust-types` (public type checklist, "wire or don't define"), `rustdoc` (doc comment format), `adr`.

- `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for the consumer API.
- No wildcard `_` arm on enums this crate owns; a compile error on a new variant is the point.
- Code never cites spec, criterion or plan IDs (`SPEC-001`, `AC-007`, `T-009`). Specs change; the code says what it guarantees in its own words, and tests name the behavior they prove.

## Testing

- `cargo nextest` plus `cargo test --doc`. `insta` for snapshots: accept a snapshot change only after confirming the new output is correct, not just different.
- Assert content, not presence: `assert_eq!` on the exact value over `contains`/`is_some`.
- Sibling-path parity: a function that mirrors an already-tested one gets a test asserting the same contract.
- CI gates line coverage at 90%.

## Fixing bugs

Look for structurally identical siblings and fix them in the same change. If one is deliberately left, say where and why.

When the spec itself is wrong, fix the spec file and add an entry to [`05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md) explaining what was wrong and why the fix is right. A decision that departs from the spec with a credible alternative gets an ADR.

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md).
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions.
- Comments explain only the non-obvious why, carry no history (the commit records it), and fill to 120 columns.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why. Skip the body when the subject says it all.

1	# Wisp
2	
3	- **Status:** early implementation in the working tree; release readiness has not been established.
4	- **Purpose:** local-first project intelligence for coding agents and humans.
5	
6	Wisp makes a repository's durable project knowledge usable without relying on a conversation's context window. It joins four kinds of evidence:
7	
8	1. canonical, Git-tracked work artifacts such as specifications, plans, architecture models, and decisions;
9	2. current repository and historical evidence from Git;
10	3. structural code evidence supplied by [Monokl](../monokl/README.md); and
11	4. an explicitly rebuildable local index and briefing cache.
12	
13	Wisp is not an agent runtime, a replacement for Git, a code parser, or an opaque "AI memory" product. It is a library with a CLI first and an MCP server as a thin later surface. Its job is to answer evidence-backed project questions and prepare a small, relevant context package for a particular stage of work.
14	
15	## The central rule
16	
17	The cache is never the authority.
18	
19	```text
20	Git-tracked artifacts + Git state + Monokl code evidence
21	                         │
22	                         ▼
23	               Wisp's rebuildable index/cache
24	                         │
25	                         ▼
26	             CLI / MCP evidence-backed response
27	```
28	
29	If `.wisp/` is deleted, Wisp must be able to reconstruct it from the workspace. If Wisp is absent, a harness must still be able to read the documented JSON artifacts directly and carry out the portable baseline workflow.
30	
31	## Repository reading order
32	
33	Start with [Implementation handoff MVP](docs/05-implementation-handoff-mvp.md) for the implemented core, its remaining integration/value gates, failure cases, and evidence required before expanding it.
34	
35	1. [Vision and boundaries](docs/01-vision-and-boundaries.md)
36	2. [Architecture and contracts](docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md)
37	3. [Delivery plan and acceptance gates](docs/03-delivery-plan.md)
38	4. [Decision log and open questions](docs/04-decisions-and-open-questions.md)
39	
40	Accepted architectural decisions are indexed in [docs/adr](docs/adr/README.md).
41	
42	## Available in the working tree
43	
44	The CLI implements these spec-only commands; they are not a claim that the acceptance gates have passed:
45	
46	```bash
47	cargo run -p wisp-cli -- artifact validate fixtures/spec-valid.json
48	cargo run -p wisp-cli -- artifact persist candidate.json --workspace .
49	cargo run -p wisp-cli -- artifact get WISP-001 --workspace .
50	cargo run -p wisp-cli -- artifact status WISP-001 --workspace .
51	```
52	
53	`persist` writes a canonical spec but does not commit it. The schema library embeds six canonical artifact contracts plus the transient `implementation-context@1` response contract. The artifact library supports read-only discovery, one-hop context assembly, and explicit selected task/batch assembly. Task-specific harness consumption, code evidence, SQLite, MCP, and service mode remain planned.
54	
55	## Bounded implementation context
56	
57	```text
58	Claude / Codex / OpenCode / a human
59	              │
60	              ▼
61	      wisp brief implement --workspace . --plan docs/projects/SPEC-001.json --batch B1
62	              │
63	              ▼
64	  checked plan/spec relationship + exact selected tasks/criteria
65	  + source digests + explicit gaps
66	```
67	
68	The command validates the selected plan/spec chain and returns a bounded JSON envelope. Each source is capped at 1 MiB. The Rust library exposes typed selection and error values; the CLI adapts failures to the stable JSON contract. It is read-only and cache-free: it does not run tests, choose batches, grant approval, or query Monokl. Smith may consume a successful packet as artifact context; normal code inspection and verification remain required. The optional integration preserves native fallback and drift behavior. A controlled value evaluation remains pending.
69	
70	## Related projects
71	
72	- **Monokl** supplies AST-aware code evidence, code search, symbols, definitions, references, and precision metadata. Wisp must not duplicate its parser, AST cache, or code index.
73	- **Michi** is a future optional presentation adapter. The MVP has no Michi dependency; proposed decision D-029 narrows its release gate to features that use it.

# Wisp

- **Status:** early implementation in the working tree; release readiness has not been established.
- **Purpose:** local-first project intelligence for coding agents and humans.

Wisp makes a repository's durable project knowledge usable without relying on a conversation's context window. It joins four kinds of evidence:

1. canonical, Git-tracked work artifacts such as specifications, plans, architecture models, and decisions;
2. current repository and historical evidence from Git;
3. structural code evidence supplied by [Monokl](../monokl/README.md); and
4. an explicitly rebuildable local index and briefing cache.

Wisp is not an agent runtime, a replacement for Git, a code parser, or an opaque "AI memory" product. It is a library with a CLI first and an MCP server as a thin later surface. Its job is to answer evidence-backed project questions and prepare a small, relevant context package for a particular stage of work.

## The central rule

The cache is never the authority.

```text
Git-tracked artifacts + Git state + Monokl code evidence
                         │
                         ▼
               Wisp's rebuildable index/cache
                         │
                         ▼
             CLI / MCP evidence-backed response
```

If `.wisp/` is deleted, Wisp must be able to reconstruct it from the workspace. If Wisp is absent, a harness must still be able to read the documented JSON artifacts directly and carry out the portable baseline workflow.

## Repository reading order

Start with [Implementation handoff MVP](docs/05-implementation-handoff-mvp.md) for the implemented core, its remaining integration/value gates, failure cases, and evidence required before expanding it.

1. [Vision and boundaries](docs/01-vision-and-boundaries.md)
2. [Architecture and contracts](docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md)
3. [Delivery plan and acceptance gates](docs/03-delivery-plan.md)
4. [Decision log and open questions](docs/04-decisions-and-open-questions.md)

Accepted architectural decisions are indexed in [docs/adr](docs/adr/README.md).

## Available in the working tree

The CLI implements these spec-only commands; they are not a claim that the acceptance gates have passed:

```bash
cargo run -p wisp-cli -- artifact validate fixtures/spec-valid.json
cargo run -p wisp-cli -- artifact persist candidate.json --workspace .
cargo run -p wisp-cli -- artifact get WISP-001 --workspace .
cargo run -p wisp-cli -- artifact status WISP-001 --workspace .
```

`persist` writes a canonical spec but does not commit it. The schema library embeds six canonical artifact contracts plus the transient `implementation-context@1` response contract. The artifact library supports read-only discovery, one-hop context assembly, and explicit selected task/batch assembly. Task-specific harness consumption, code evidence, SQLite, MCP, and service mode remain planned.

## Bounded implementation context

```text
Claude / Codex / OpenCode / a human
              │
              ▼
      wisp brief implement --workspace . --plan docs/projects/SPEC-001.json --batch B1
              │
              ▼
  checked plan/spec relationship + exact selected tasks/criteria
  + source digests + explicit gaps
```

The command validates the selected plan/spec chain and returns a bounded JSON envelope. Each source is capped at 1 MiB. The Rust library exposes typed selection and error values; the CLI adapts failures to the stable JSON contract. It is read-only and cache-free: it does not run tests, choose batches, grant approval, or query Monokl. Smith may consume a successful packet as artifact context; normal code inspection and verification remain required. The optional integration preserves native fallback and drift behavior. A controlled value evaluation remains pending.

## Related projects

- **Monokl** supplies AST-aware code evidence, code search, symbols, definitions, references, and precision metadata. Wisp must not duplicate its parser, AST cache, or code index.
- **Michi** is a future optional presentation adapter. The MVP has no Michi dependency; proposed decision D-029 narrows its release gate to features that use it.
- **Callisto** offers precedents for authorized effects, typed observations, receipts, and crash-safe writes. Its current Git access uses subprocesses; no standalone `callisto-vcs` dependency is assumed. Check API and license compatibility before code reuse.
- **Lumen** observes agent sessions, cache use, and retrieval loops. It is an evaluation/telemetry companion, never project truth.
- **Prism** evaluates whether Wisp context actually improves task success, correctness, latency, and cost across harnesses.

See [Architecture and contracts](docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md) for the precise boundaries.

1	# Default recipe: fast local CI pipeline (no coverage) via moon & just.
2	# Use `just ci` explicitly for full CI parity including coverage.
3	default: ci
4	
5	# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
6	build:
7	    moon run :build
8	
9	# Build release CLI binary
10	build-release:
11	    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli
12	
13	# Time `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and count their git processes.
14	# `CALLISTO_BENCH_PACKAGES=50,200` picks the sizes.
15	bench:
16	    cargo bench -p callisto-cli --bench commands
17	
18	# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests. This intentionally uses the
19	# same Nextest command as CI: a runner/configuration failure must never be
20	# mistaken for a passing Moon fallback.
21	test:
22	    cargo nextest run --workspace
23	    cargo test --doc --workspace
24	
25	# Explicit compatibility path for contributors who do not have cargo-nextest
26	# installed. It is never used by CI or pre-merge verification.
27	test-moon:
28	    moon run :test
29	    cargo test --doc --workspace
30	
31	# Exercise the Release-PR action's shell block with Git and GitHub faked; it never calls the real binary (see test-release-action-binary).
32	test-release-action:
33	    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh
34	
35	# Compiles callisto and runs the Release-PR action's jq extraction against
36	# its real JSON output. Requires pending changesets to exercise update and
37	# supersede decisions; skips cleanly otherwise.
38	test-release-action-binary:
39	    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh
40	
41	# Compiles callisto and feeds its real error output through the CI problem matcher.
42	test-problem-matcher:
43	    bash .github/tests/test-problem-matcher.sh
44	
45	# Execute the release lifecycle at the real CLI boundary with fake registry,
46	# Git, forge, and attestation providers. This is deliberately separate from
47	# broad workspace tests so PR CI makes the release behavior evidence visible.
48	release-workflow-behavior:
49	    bash .github/tests/release-workflow-behavior/run.sh
50	
51	# Re-captures the real provider responses under testing/fixtures/providers with
52	# read-only network GETs. Manual: review the diff and update PROVENANCE.md.
53	provider-fixtures:
54	    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh
55	
56	# Manual and network-dependent, so deliberately not part of `ci`: re-fetches the
57	# live providers and asserts each fixture's SHAPE (status code, JSON key paths,
58	# ls-remote line kinds) still matches; content is never compared.
59	provider-contract:
60	    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh --check
61	
62	# Reject history words and plain comment blocks over three lines (`comment-block-ok` marks an exception).
63	check-comments:
64	    bash testing/check-comments.sh
65	
66	# Clippy as one workspace invocation: moon's per-project runs serialize on cargo's shared target/ lock.
67	lint: check-comments
68	    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
69	    cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used
70	
71	# Lint only moon-affected projects, in one cargo invocation to avoid the build-lock serialization.
72	lint-affected:
73	    #!/usr/bin/env bash
74	    set -euo pipefail
75	    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
76	    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
77	        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
78	        exit 0
79	    fi
80	    args=()
81	    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
82	    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings
83	    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used
84	
85	# Check code formatting compliance via moon
86	fmt-check:
87	    moon run :format-check
88	
89	# Format code automatically via moon
90	fmt:
91	    moon run :format
92	
93	# Security advisory, ban, license & source check via cargo-deny (workspace root, one pass)
94	audit: license-boundary
95	    cargo deny check
96	
97	# callisto-model is MIT: nothing it depends on at build or run time, directly or not, may be FSL-licensed or a Callisto FSL crate.
98	license-boundary:
99	    ! cargo tree -p callisto-model -e normal,build --prefix none --format '{p} {l}' | grep -E 'FSL|callisto-(manifests|graph|cli|fixtures)'
100	
101	# Compile the fuzz targets so they cannot rot (running them needs nightly and cargo-fuzz)
102	fuzz-check:
103	    cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins
104	
105	# Run mutation testing sweep via cargo-mutants
106	mutants:
107	    cargo mutants --workspace
108	
109	# The shipped binary is built with the features its crates default to, and none of them is the dev-only `test-util`.
110	features-boundary:
111	    ! cargo tree -p callisto-cli -e normal,build -f '{p} {f}' | grep 'test-util'
112	
113	# Run unused dependency check via cargo-machete
114	machete:
115	    cargo machete
116	
117	# Verify public Rust API SemVer breaking changes
118	check-api:
119	    cargo semver-checks check-release
120	
121	# Run structure-aware fuzzing target
122	fuzz target="parse_package_id":
123	    cargo fuzz run {{target}}
124	
125	# Documentation build check (warnings treated as errors)
126	doc-check:
127	    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace
128	
129	# Coverage via cargo-llvm-cov; a `threshold` fails below that line coverage, after printing the summary.
130	# `just ci` and CI both call `just coverage 90`, so a CI failure reproduces locally.
131	coverage threshold="":
132	    #!/usr/bin/env bash
133	    set -euo pipefail
134	    args=(--workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info)
135	    cargo llvm-cov "${args[@]}"
136	    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
137	    if [[ -n "{{threshold}}" ]]; then
138	      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{threshold}}"
139	    fi
140	
141	# Per-crate line coverage against a threshold (default 90%): the workspace total can pass while a small crate is far below.
142	# Needs profile data from a prior `cargo llvm-cov` run; it does not re-run tests.
143	coverage-per-crate threshold="90":
144	    #!/usr/bin/env bash
145	    set -euo pipefail
146	    cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only > /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json
147	    report=$(jq -r '
148	        .data[0].files[]
149	        | select(.filename | test("/crates/"))
150	        | {crate: (.filename | capture("/crates/(?<c>[^/]+)/").c), count: .summary.lines.count, covered: .summary.lines.covered}
151	        | [.crate, .count, .covered]
152	        | @tsv
153	      ' /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json \
154	      | awk -F'\t' -v threshold="{{threshold}}" '
155	          {sum[$1]+=$2; cov[$1]+=$3}
156	          END {
157	            for (c in sum) {
158	              pct = (cov[c]/sum[c]*100)
159	              status = (pct+0 < threshold+0) ? "FAIL" : "pass"
160	              printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%.2f\t%s\n", c, sum[c], cov[c], pct, status
161	            }
162	          }
163	        ' | sort)
164	    echo "$report" | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%-25s lines=%-6s covered=%-6s cover=%6s%%  %s\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5}'
165	    echo "$report" | grep -q FAIL && exit 1 || exit 0
166	
167	# Clean build targets, Moon task caches, and generated artifacts
168	clean:
169	    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
170	    cargo clean
171	    rm -f lcov.info callisto-schema.json
172	
173	# Fast pre-commit hook validation (<500ms formatting check)
174	pre-commit: fmt-check
175	
176	# Pre-push hook validation: formatting check plus clippy on affected projects only
177	pre-push: fmt-check lint-affected
178	
179	# Install native Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks
180	hooks:
181	    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-commit' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
182	    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
183	    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-push' > .git/hooks/pre-push
184	    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push
185	    @echo "Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks installed successfully."
186	
187	# Static security audit of workflows and actions (requires zizmor and ripgrep).
188	zizmor:
189	    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .
190	
191	# Credential-free release workflow contract, policy, and policy mutant checks.
192	release-workflow-checks:
193	    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh
194	    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh
195	
196	# Workflow Contracts CI job minus actionlint and zizmor: pins, release
197	# contract/policy, artifact build script, the Release-PR action contract
198	# under a minimal PATH, and the installer verification-mode tests.
199	workflow-contracts: release-workflow-checks
200	    bash .github/tests/test_release_candidate_recovery.sh
201	    bash .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh
202	    bash .github/tests/test-release-artifact-build-script.sh
203	    bash .github/tests/test-move-floating-tag.sh

# Default recipe: fast local CI pipeline (no coverage) via moon & just.
# Use `just ci` explicitly for full CI parity including coverage.
default: ci

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:
    moon run :build

# Build release CLI binary
build-release:
    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli

# Time `status`, `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` over generated workspaces and count their git processes.
# `CALLISTO_BENCH_PACKAGES=50,200` picks the sizes.
bench:
    cargo bench -p callisto-cli --bench commands

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests. This intentionally uses the
# same Nextest command as CI: a runner/configuration failure must never be
# mistaken for a passing Moon fallback.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Explicit compatibility path for contributors who do not have cargo-nextest
# installed. It is never used by CI or pre-merge verification.
test-moon:
    moon run :test
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Exercise the Release-PR action's shell block with Git and GitHub faked; it never calls the real binary (see test-release-action-binary).
test-release-action:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and runs the Release-PR action's jq extraction against
# its real JSON output. Requires pending changesets to exercise update and
# supersede decisions; skips cleanly otherwise.
test-release-action-binary:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and feeds its real error output through the CI problem matcher.
test-problem-matcher:
    bash .github/tests/test-problem-matcher.sh

# Execute the release lifecycle at the real CLI boundary with fake registry,
# Git, forge, and attestation providers. This is deliberately separate from
# broad workspace tests so PR CI makes the release behavior evidence visible.
release-workflow-behavior:
    bash .github/tests/release-workflow-behavior/run.sh

# Re-captures the real provider responses under testing/fixtures/providers with
# read-only network GETs. Manual: review the diff and update PROVENANCE.md.
provider-fixtures:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh

# Manual and network-dependent, so deliberately not part of `ci`: re-fetches the
# live providers and asserts each fixture's SHAPE (status code, JSON key paths,
# ls-remote line kinds) still matches; content is never compared.
provider-contract:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh --check

# Reject history words and plain comment blocks over three lines (`comment-block-ok` marks an exception).
check-comments:
    bash testing/check-comments.sh

# Clippy as one workspace invocation: moon's per-project runs serialize on cargo's shared target/ lock.
lint: check-comments
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used

# Lint only moon-affected projects, in one cargo invocation to avoid the build-lock serialization.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used

# Check code formatting compliance via moon
fmt-check:
    moon run :format-check

# Format code automatically via moon
fmt:
    moon run :format

# Security advisory, ban, license & source check via cargo-deny (workspace root, one pass)
audit: license-boundary
    cargo deny check

# callisto-model is MIT: nothing it depends on at build or run time, directly or not, may be FSL-licensed or a Callisto FSL crate.
license-boundary:
    ! cargo tree -p callisto-model -e normal,build --prefix none --format '{p} {l}' | grep -E 'FSL|callisto-(manifests|graph|cli|fixtures)'

# Compile the fuzz targets so they cannot rot (running them needs nightly and cargo-fuzz)
fuzz-check:
    cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins

# Run mutation testing sweep via cargo-mutants
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# The shipped binary is built with the features its crates default to, and none of them is the dev-only `test-util`.
features-boundary:
    ! cargo tree -p callisto-cli -e normal,build -f '{p} {f}' | grep 'test-util'

# Run unused dependency check via cargo-machete
machete:
    cargo machete

# Verify public Rust API SemVer breaking changes
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Run structure-aware fuzzing target
fuzz target="parse_package_id":
    cargo fuzz run {{target}}

# Documentation build check (warnings treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace

# Coverage via cargo-llvm-cov; a `threshold` fails below that line coverage, after printing the summary.
# `just ci` and CI both call `just coverage 90`, so a CI failure reproduces locally.
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    args=(--workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info)
    cargo llvm-cov "${args[@]}"
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{threshold}}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{threshold}}"
    fi

# Per-crate line coverage against a threshold (default 90%): the workspace total can pass while a small crate is far below.
# Needs profile data from a prior `cargo llvm-cov` run; it does not re-run tests.
coverage-per-crate threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only > /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json
    report=$(jq -r '
        .data[0].files[]
        | select(.filename | test("/crates/"))
        | {crate: (.filename | capture("/crates/(?<c>[^/]+)/").c), count: .summary.lines.count, covered: .summary.lines.covered}
        | [.crate, .count, .covered]
        | @tsv
      ' /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json \
      | awk -F'\t' -v threshold="{{threshold}}" '
          {sum[$1]+=$2; cov[$1]+=$3}
          END {
            for (c in sum) {
              pct = (cov[c]/sum[c]*100)
              status = (pct+0 < threshold+0) ? "FAIL" : "pass"
              printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%.2f\t%s\n", c, sum[c], cov[c], pct, status
            }
          }
        ' | sort)
    echo "$report" | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%-25s lines=%-6s covered=%-6s cover=%6s%%  %s\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5}'
    echo "$report" | grep -q FAIL && exit 1 || exit 0

# Clean build targets, Moon task caches, and generated artifacts
clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean
    rm -f lcov.info callisto-schema.json

# Fast pre-commit hook validation (<500ms formatting check)
pre-commit: fmt-check

# Pre-push hook validation: formatting check plus clippy on affected projects only
pre-push: fmt-check lint-affected

# Install native Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks
hooks:
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-commit' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-push' > .git/hooks/pre-push
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push
    @echo "Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks installed successfully."

# Static security audit of workflows and actions (requires zizmor and ripgrep).
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Credential-free release workflow contract, policy, and policy mutant checks.
release-workflow-checks:
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh

# Workflow Contracts CI job minus actionlint and zizmor: pins, release
# contract/policy, artifact build script, the Release-PR action contract
# under a minimal PATH, and the installer verification-mode tests.
workflow-contracts: release-workflow-checks
    bash .github/tests/test_release_candidate_recovery.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-release-artifact-build-script.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-move-floating-tag.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-hold-release-pr.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_contract.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_download_extraction_format.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_action_ref_version_resolution.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_crates_io_fallback.sh

# Every check CI runs except actionlint (Docker) and the binary-dependent
# release-PR decide contract, problem matcher contract and artifact preflight build. CI runs them as
# parallel jobs (callisto-ci.yml); locally they run in sequence.
ci: fmt-check lint fuzz-check test audit doc-check zizmor workflow-contracts release-workflow-behavior (coverage "90")

391	      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
392	        with:
393	          name: release-intent
394	          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
395	      # Every matrix target's artifact, so a target added to the matrix cannot be built and then left out of the manifest.
396	      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
397	        with:
